card: Trail length per generation (BP-DX=400h): test 300h/500h/800h variants (keep coverage), anchor dwell exposure vs rebuild overhead.

model.results: Partner kills of A by B over 25 band combos: 400h 11/25, 300h 4/25, 500h 15/25, 800h 0/25; B never killed by A. Chaotic, at most ~0.004/battle per A005; not decisive.

candidates.label: A_t800
candidates.change: A only: phoenix mov dx,04000h -> 03C00h (trail per generation 800h, BP 4400h step and 52h lattice kept, full coverage kept; B = base)
candidates.notes: Screen helped: MOVSW threats (cgx123123 +0.2, CodeKiller +0.17, Baltika9 +0.1), lead_zrl03 +0.11, lead_ah02 +0.10, zchain4 +0.07. Regressed: strong group -0.068 (not significant, 2/5), lead_V6 -0.128 in screen but +0.010 in the independent threat job. Threat job (fresh seeds/fills) replicates cgx123123 (+0.16, 4/0) and zrl03 (+0.125, 4/0). Neighbours 500h and 300h are clearly negative, so the response to trail length is non-monotonic/chaotic; 800h result could partly be screen luck.

threatFindings.threat: Shorter A trail (300h) reduces dwell exposure enough to pay for the extra rebuilds and lost coverage
Trail length is a monotonic dwell-vs-rebuild trade-off
threatFindings.evidence: 300h -0.031, 500h -0.033 (strong -0.113 [-0.174,-0.051]), 800h +0.016 around the 400h base: non-monotonic; 500h is clearly worse than both 400h and 800h, so geometry (where the trail end lands relative to the next lattice point, 400h-800h above anchor) matters more than dwell/rebuild ratio.

threatFindings.threat: A 800h trail (sweeping the next 52h-lattice point and the 400h above it) helps vs MOVSW-family cgx123123 and vs combo_zrl03
threatFindings.impact: +0.05 on the threat subset; mechanism (which bytes kill them) untraced = hypothesis
